title: Quantile-Coupled Flow Matching for Distributional Reinforcement Learning
claim: Arbitrary source-target pairing yields crossing paths and higher transport cost; sorted coupling gives monotone, non-crossing transport and lower cost.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: prior, ours, bar chart; colored coupling lines
description: Three-part figure with a shared quantile x-axis. On the far left, a small source distribution (uniform-looking scatter in viridis colors) feeds the left panel, titled 'Standard CFM (Arbitrary Coupling)'. That panel shows a solid black source line g(τ) and a dashed black target quantile curve, joined by many tangled, crossing multicolor lines. A thick pink line carries a pink-boxed |F⁻¹(τ')−g(τ)| label. A mixed-color bimodal target density sits beside it. The middle panel, 'FlowIQN (Sorted Coupling)', has the same two curves joined by neat, parallel, non-crossing gradient lines. A green vertical segment carries a green-boxed label. Its bimodal target density is ordered by color. On the right, a bar chart of expected transport cost compares a hatched pink Standard CFM bar with a shorter green FlowIQN bar, labeled '1.2x Loss'. The double-integral formula sits above the bar chart. The eye goes first to the tangled lines, then to the clean ones.
caption: FlowIQN aligns flow matching with Wasserstein geometry. (Left) Standard CFM arbitrarily couples source and target quantiles (τ, τ ′). This metric mismatch produces crossing paths and a double-integral expected cost that is not a Wasserstein projection. (Center & Right) FlowIQN’s quantile coupling (τ ≈τ ′) approximates the 1D monotone optimal transport map. Because sorting pairs samples by their rank order, it explicitly transports each source quantile toward its exact corresponding target quantile. This monotone constraint ensures the regression objective upper-bounds, up to a constant, the 1D squared 2-Wasserstein distance, so that minimising the flow-matching loss is an approximate Wasserstein projection of the Bellman target.
abstract: Distributional Reinforcement Learning (DRL) models the full return distribution, making it well-suited to uncertainty-aware and risk-sensitive decision-making. Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) critics are increasingly adopted in DRL, offering dense velocity supervision and a natural axis for scaling critic computation. Yet they carry a hidden metric mismatch: the distributional Bellman operator is a contraction in the Wasserstein distance, but CFM critics pair source and Bellman target samples arbitrarily, so their loss does not control the Wasserstein distance to the Bellman target. We show that this mismatch can be fixed with a single sorting operation. Our method, FlowIQN, sorts source and target samples within each mini-batch so that each source quantile is transported to its matching target quantile, approximating the monotone optimal transport coupling. We prove that this quantile coupling makes the CFM loss upper-bound, up to a constant, the squared 2-Wasserstein projection error. To our knowledge, this makes FlowIQN the first flow-matching critic whose training is an approximate Wasserstein projection of the Bellman target, and the guarantee extends to shortcut models for few-step inference. Empirically, the quantile coupling recovers multi-modal returns more accurately than an otherwise identical uncoupled flow with as few as two integration steps. FlowIQN improves substantially on the flow critic Value Flows in a fixed-policy diagnostic and is competitive on offline RL benchmarks across multiple policy extraction methods, identifying the coupling as a central design axis for flow-based critics. Code: https://github.com/ori-goals/flowIQN
